To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) leakage power can differ by up to 3X for temperatures between room temperature and 110°C; (2) leakage energy is the primary contributor to system energy, and leakage energy is highly sensitive to temperature; (3) the interdependence between dynamic leakage power and temperature can cause thermal runaway, which is a major problem in future systems; and (4) direct water-spray active cooling can significantly reduce thermal resistance and increase system maximum clock rate.

(1) temperature has a strong influence on leakage power, (2) leakage power can be different by as much as 10X for a 75°C change, (3) temperature can be different by 20°C between two processors running the same application, and (4) leakage power and temperature form an interdependent loop that can lead to thermal runaway.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the interdependence between power and thermal simulation.
the accurate power simulation, thermal simulation, and the thermal management techniques for the future high-performance systems.
the accurate simulation of coupled power and thermal effects in modern microprocessors, which is critical for the development of future microprocessors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
power and thermal management is a very challenging problem for future systems.
power simulation without considering temperature calculation is inaccurate and that thermal simulation without considering leakage power and voltage scaling is incomplete.
power is a major design constraint and thermal simulation is essential in modern microarchitecture design.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
power simulation must include thermal calculation, and thermal simulation must consider power.
power simulation without thermal simulation is not accurate, and active cooling is a promising technique that can significantly increase microprocessor performance.
power and thermal simulation should be considered together, especially when leakage power and temperature dependent leakage power are significant.
The main takeaway from our work is that
thermal and power simulation are coupled, and that leakage power is highly sensitive to temperature, which can lead to severe thermal runaway.
the coupled thermal management and power management is critical for future microprocessor and system design.
power simulation without temperature calculation and thermal management is inaccurate.
